title: Heap schism: KV index replay + OOM throttler for bursty inference workloads
creator: Evelyn Kim
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated) observed hard GPU OOMs during short, high-concurrency inference spikes combined with long-running sessions. Investigation points to a combination of fragmented heap arenas and stale KV-index entries that prevent efficient reclaim; when the runtime attempts to replay session KV indices after free/list churn, it transiently duplicates in-memory descriptors and inflates ephemeral allocations. The result is rapid headroom loss on GPUs serving bursty workloads, leading to throttled requests and some customer escalations in Private/VPC tenants where memory budgets are conservative.

This ticket covers: triage timeline, mitigations, a minimal runtime patch (index-replay dedupe + OOM soft-throttle), rollout plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, verification criteria, and follow-ups (postmortem + long-term allocator redesign).
comments: 2025-02-10 09:12 - Evelyn Kim: Triage call summary. Customer A (hosted) and Customer B (dedicated) reported 5xx errors and telemetry showing node GPU memory pinned near 100% within 30s of a sudden traffic spike. Both clusters show high session churn. Captured debug dumps from two affected nodes (node ids attached). Initial hypothesis: stale KV-index replay + arena fragmentation. Assigning to Marco to reproduce locally with synthetic burst harness.

2025-02-11 14:30 - Marco Alvarez: Repro achieved in synthetic harness by running 500 concurrent short chat sessions that perform alternating long and short context expansions. Heap snapshots show repeated allocation of KV descriptor objects during index replay; a race in the replay path allows duplicate descriptors to be retained transiently due to missing CAS when swapping reconciliation pointers. Created a short, targeted runtime patch that deduplicates descriptors at the head of the replay loop and adds a soft OOM throttle (slow-path backoff) to shed load while reclaim completes. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7802

2025-02-12 10:05 - SRE (Ruth Patel): Canary plan proposed: roll patch to 2 non-prod clusters, enable verbose mem-trace, warmup with historical customer traffic patterns, then canary into one hosted region and one dedicated pool with low-risk tenants. For Private customers we'll provide the patch as an offline hotpatch bundle and coordinate upgrade windows.

2025-02-12 17:48 - Product (Liam O'Reilly): Noted several enterprise customers require an audit log entry and changelog. Add release notes describing behavior change and documented rollback steps. Ensure upgrade path preserves pinned model versions.

2025-02-13 08:22 - Marco Alvarez: PR updated with unit tests that simulate concurrent replay and assert no duplicate descriptor creation. Also added metrics (runtime.kv.replay_duplicates_count, runtime.kv.replay_dedupe_latency_ms) and an admin flag runtime.kv.replay_dedupe_enabled for staged rollout. Observability dashboard draft: grafana/runtime/kv-replay-heatmap (link in attachments).

2025-02-14 11:05 - Evelyn Kim: After successful canaries (24h) we observed elimination of transient duplication in canary nodes and reduction of GPU OOM spikes from 7 incidents/day to 0 on canary pool. SRE recommends progressive rollout. Next: schedule Private/VPC customer patch windows and coordinate with Support for post-upgrade verification.

2025-02-14 15:00 - Marco Alvarez: Rolling patch to hosted region us-west-2 and dedicated-pool-3 with a staged ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 6h. Runbook trigger: if runtime.kv.replay_duplicates_count > 1 or GPU memory RSS increases > 25% baseline during ramp, abort and rollback to previous runtime.
verification_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 candidate to canary cluster with runtime.kv.replay_dedupe_enabled=true and mem-tracing enabled. 2) Re-run bursty inference harness used in repro and assert runtime.kv.replay_duplicates_count == 0 for 1000 runs. 3) Monitor GPU RSS and runtime.kv.replay_dedupe_latency_ms; 95th pct latency must remain < 50ms. 4) After 24h of stable canary, ramp to 50% and then 100% following SRE rollout policy. 5) For Private customers, provide hotpatch bundle and coordinate verification: run in staging and confirm same metrics before scheduling production window.
rollback_plan: Rollback is safe: flip admin flag runtime.kv.replay_dedupe_enabled=false and redeploy previous runtime binary if severe regressions observed. Pre-built previous runtime images available: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:1.19.7-backup. Support to pause model rollouts on affected nodes during rollback.
postmortem_actions: - Complete full postmortem doc within 7 days (owner: Evelyn). - Add CI fuzz test for index-replay concurrency (owner: Marco). - Evaluate allocator improvements to reduce fragmentation and add slab compaction telemetry (owner: infra team). - Investigate KV-index journaling to avoid full replays where possible. - Update runbook with new metrics and clear SLO thresholds for OOM early-warning.
notes: Decision tradeoffs: the chosen fix is intentionally minimal (dedupe + soft throttle) to reduce blast radius and allow rapid rollout. Long-term fixes (allocator rewrite, journaled indices) are scoped as follow-ups to avoid blocking immediate customer relief. Private deployments will receive the same minimal patch but require coordinated windows and manual approval per customer security/compliance guidelines.
